Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary from the call:
- FintechCorp requirements: SOC 2 evidence, GDPR data processing terms, and confirmation on HIPAA controls for specific PII/PHI flows.
- Incident response: FintechCorp requires breach notification SLA and evidence of IR runbooks and on-call process.
- BCP/DR: RTO/RPO expectations and recent DR test results are requested.

Action items we agreed on:
1) FintechCorp to share the vendor security questionnaire (or we can send ours) — target: EOW 9/17.
2) Redwood to provide current SOC 2 status and a concise summary (we can provide a bridge letter if full Type II report pending).
3) Redwood to share IR playbook excerpt and BCP test evidence.
4) Schedule a follow-up with our security lead to walk the questionnaire and any gaps — propose Tue 9/15 or Wed 9/16.

For visibility, attaching a short Redwood security one-pager that outlines our controls and where SOC 2 documentation will sit.

Attachments: redwood_security_onepager.pdf (application/pdf, 95KB)

Next steps from my side: I’ll drop the SOC 2 summary and our IR playbook into the shared folder and ping you when it’s ready. Please send over the questionnaire or let me know if you want us to kick off with our standard vendor questionnaire.

Best,

Thanks Jordan — helpful recap. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- SOC 2: We need either a current Type II report or a bridge letter + a clear remediation timeline if any controls are in progress. Our procurement requires the report for legal sign-off.
- Breach notification: Our policy requires vendor notification within 72 hours of confirming a breach affecting customer data. We will escalate faster for critical incidents.
- GDPR / HIPAA: We have specific DPA language for GDPR and a BAA for HIPAA. We can share the required clauses — you should confirm you can accept those.
- Evidence: IR runbook, timeline for detection/containment/notification, and results from the most recent BCP/DR test (last 12 months).

We’ll attach the vendor questionnaire in a separate email today. Can you confirm what Redwood’s standard notification timeline is (i.e., how many hours after detection do you notify affected customers) and who the on-call contact for IR is?

Appreciate it — Sara
Sara Lim

Jordan / Laura — quick internal note before we respond to Tom/Sara: 

- Notification SLA: Legal has historically pushed for 24 hours for confirmed incidents affecting customer data; Ops/security are comfortable with 48 hours for confirmed incidents and initial notification within 24 hours for critical P0 incidents. For procurement we can accept a 72-hour contractual initial notification SLA — that aligns with our escalation playbooks and gives DevOps time to validate.

- On-call monitoring: incident-response@redwood.com routes to PagerDuty; the mailbox is monitored and the primary on-call rotation is the platform SRE team (contact: +1 (650) 555-0142). We should include a named on-call lead when we hand this to FintechCorp (I can volunteer to be the primary contact for the first 30 days).

- Evidence: We can provide the bridge letter + control evidence set and the Q2 DR test results. Recommend we redact any internal-only entries in the DR workbook before sending.

Recommend reply to FintechCorp: confirm we will contractually commit to 72-hour initial notification, provide the incident-response contact and PagerDuty escalation, attach the IR playbook excerpt and DR test summary, and propose Tue 9/15 10am PT for a walk-through.
